title: Even so: a pesar de and pese a

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *a pesar de* + noun or infinitive, *a pesar de que* + a clause and *pese a* from B1 Unit 32. They admit a difficulty and go on. They suit the story of new democracies, where courts and laws existed but did not always work as promised.

items.spanish: A pesar de las nuevas constituciones, muchos jueces seguían dependiendo de los gobiernos.
items.english: Despite the new constitutions, many judges still depended on the governments.

items.spanish: A pesar de que la ley reconocía los derechos, mucha gente no podía defenderlos.
items.english: Although the law recognised rights, many people could not defend them.

items.spanish: Pese a algunos problemas, mucha gente usó la tutela.
items.english: Despite some problems, many people used the tutela.

items.spanish: A pesar de ser un recurso sencillo, la tutela fue muy usada.
items.english: Despite being a simple remedy, the tutela was widely used.

sections.content: After *a pesar de* put a noun or an infinitive (*a pesar de ser sencillo*); before a full clause use *a pesar de que*, with the indicative for a real fact. *Pese a* + noun means the same as *a pesar de*.
